data.why: The repo ships a built-in CC BY 4.0 five-session HDF5 database (examples/Mouse56_5sessions.mat) made for manual browser validation of exactly this workflow, so the start command preloads it with --database and no synthetic data is needed.

goals: import a CaImAn/Minian/MIN1PIPE segmentation result into a portable HDF5 cell database
review per-cell quality metrics (footprint area, eccentricity, temporal contrast) and discard noisy or doubled-up ROIs
merge over-segmented ROIs that represent a single cell within one session
align fields of view across imaging sessions to correct for motion/drift between days
match the same cells across sessions to build a cross-session registration matrix
save the cleaned, aligned, and matched result as a new curated database without altering the raw file

review.summary: This is a sound tree: it follows the dashboard's real clean/merge → align → match → save pipeline, with well-cut features and screens that mostly back the claims. It needs fixes before filing: an unreached import phase, a better place for the Raw Preview and Undo tasks, three citations that show loading screens or a cut-off file name instead of the outcome, the missing match-curation and optimizer tasks, and a split of the oversized matching feature.
